deferred.reason: The gate is branch-gated by design and refuses to run on a campaign branch: check-main-branch accepts only branch 'main' or a detached HEAD in tag-publish context, and the .gate-evidence/ records it consumes (fast, tui, arch, workflows) must name the release commit SHA and the release version. This wave's own Verify block runs the bake on a feature branch, so this gate cannot pass before the merge without faking either the branch or the evidence.

deferred.run-when: After this wave is merged and main CI is green: check out clean main at the release SHA, run the fast, tui, arch and workflows suites with --record-gate-evidence, then run the readiness gate in pre-tag context, then create the annotated v1.00.31 tag locally and run the full CI-strict preflight in tag-publish context. The tag is pushed only if all seven gates pass.

supporting-verification.affected-tests: 19 files run through the project's own runner (racket scripts/run-tests.rkt <file>) at the final head: 376 tests, 376 passed, 0 failed, 0 timeouts, every file exit 0, and 0 files reporting no test count. Raw capture: raw/version-derivation-tests.log, which carries the runner's own Tests:/Files: lines and each file's exit code, so a vacuous green is detectable rather than assumed absent. The instrument matters here and took three attempts to get right. (1) The 05:11Z capture was taken mid-repair and records test-wave-integrity-adversarial.rkt red (1/8) while the W6 matrix was still pinned to the pre-regeneration identity - review round 3 correctly read that as contradicting this claim. (2) The 21:53Z and 22:38Z re-runs used bare 'raco test', which is wrong twice over: it exits 0 even when a case fails, AND for a file whose entry point is module+ main rather than module+ test it executes nothing and still exits 0. Two of the 19 are shaped that way (test-deterministic-clock.rkt and test-wave-delivery-integrity-register.rkt), so their greens were vacuous - a pass that ran zero tests. The 21:53Z run also miscounted its own footer, matching rackunit's green '0 failure(s)' line as a failure and reporting 11 of 19; rounds 3 and 4 found these. (3) This run uses the runner whose exit code scripts/run-tests/reporting.rkt actually gates on, since failed-result? is purely 'exit code neither 0 nor 2'. A fourth false alarm came from the detector in the capture script itself, which grepped for raco test's 'N test(s) run' shape instead of the runner's 'Tests: N total' and so reported all 19 files as count-less; fixed and re-run. That is the same trap three times over - the detector, not the subject - and the same trap that hid the worker-security W2 regression in the first place.

It does NOT name the same commit as this JSON's "commit" field, and the difference is stated rather than papered over: each capture names the tree it was actually run against, because a committed artifact cannot contain the SHA of the commit that carries it. The preflight ran at the commit in "commit" above; the suite chain ran at the head named inside verify-chain.txt, which is earlier. Every commit between that head and the merge candidate changes only docs/reports/*.md prose and this directory's own JSON captures, and no test reads any of those files — which is checked, not assumed: the delta is enumerable with git diff --name-only between the two heads, and the chain's own fast suite covers the 1209 test files that do read content. Review round 1 finding 4 asked for one coherent head, and the honest form of that is a named content head plus an explicit account of the evidence-only commits that follow it, not a claim that two runs at different commits happened at the same commit.
